overall_summary: Bitcoin trades defensively as macro and geopolitics dominate, with multi-year yield highs, near-sixty percent Fed hike odds, and oil above one hundred dollars stoking inflation and risk-off pressure. Crypto-specific headlines offer limited offsets via Nasdaq’s Kraken stake, SGX perps access, and low sell-side risk, but ETF outflows and the hold at seventy-eight thousand keep the near-term bias cautious. Today’s PPI, ECB decision, and claims data will set the next tone.
key_points: Yields and Fed hike odds near 60% weigh on risk
Oil above $100 on US-Iran escalation fuels inflation fears
Institutional offsets: Nasdaq-Kraken deal, SGX perps open
BTC holds $78K; sell-side risk at one-month low

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs Post $167M Two-Day Outflows
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs saw one hundred twenty million dollars in net outflows on Wednesday, bringing the two-day total to about one hundred sixty-seven million after their strongest three-week inflow streak of twenty twenty-six. ARK twenty-one Shares led the redemptions, followed by Grayscale and BlackRock, while Morgan Stanley was the lone inflow. Traders should care because this cools the institutional bid that had been supporting price near recent highs and signals a pause in demand ahead of key inflation data.
items.impact: Near-term pressure on BTC as spot demand softens

items.title: Bitcoin Holds $78K After Liquidation Wave and Broad Retreat
items.summary: Bitcoin dropped about two percent over twenty-four hours to hold near seventy-eight thousand dollars, wiping out Wednesday's gains and sitting five percent below last week's high. Memecoins and small caps led the selloff with a ten percent memecoin index drop, while roughly three hundred eighty-six million dollars in positions were liquidated, mostly longs. Higher oil prices and rising rate-hike odds fueled the move. Traders should watch the seventy-seven to seventy-eight thousand support zone closely ahead of PPI and CPI prints that could decide the next leg.
items.impact: Range test; resolution of support decides direction into data

items.title: SGX Opens Bitcoin and Ether Perps to US Institutions
items.summary: The Singapore Exchange received CFTC authorization under Regulation forty-eight point ten, allowing US institutional investors to trade its bitcoin and ether perpetual futures for the first time. The contracts have done five point eight billion dollars in cumulative volume since launching late last year. This bridges US trading desks with Asian liquidity in a regulated venue that uses traditional margin calls instead of auto-liquidations. It expands institutional access and legitimizes crypto derivatives further.
items.impact: Adds regulated liquidity channel for US institutions

items.title: Coinbase CEO Says Bitcoin Cycle Bottom Is In
items.summary: Brian Armstrong told Bloomberg he believes bitcoin has bottomed for the current cycle and expects an uptrend over the next one to two years into the next halving. He also noted improving US regulatory clarity around the Clarity Act and potential agency rules soon. Bitcoin was trading near seventy-eight thousand at the time, well off its all-time high. This is high-profile CEO conviction that can shape institutional and retail sentiment while price consolidates.
items.impact: Positive sentiment catalyst from major exchange CEO

items.title: Nasdaq Invests $100M in Kraken Parent at $21B Value
items.summary: Nasdaq's venture arm is putting one hundred million dollars into Payward, Kraken's parent, valuing it at twenty-one billion dollars. The deal expands their partnership on tokenized Nasdaq-listed stocks that will carry the same voting rights as regular shares, with Kraken distributing them. It deepens TradFi-crypto infrastructure ties around always-on tokenized equities. This signals continued big-exchange commitment to crypto rails and tokenization despite short-term market softness.
items.impact: Validates crypto exchange infrastructure and tokenization push

items.title: Bitcoin Sell-Side Risk Hits One-Month Low
items.summary: Glassnode data shows bitcoin's sell-side risk ratio dropped to seven basis points, less than half its August peak, as long-term holders slow profit-taking. Their share of realized profits fell to forty-seven percent from eighty-eight percent, and a large block of coins bought higher remains largely unmoved. Selling pressure is quiet even as price sits below the eighty-three to eighty-six thousand resistance band. This on-chain calm reduces overhead supply risk if buyers step back in after data.
items.impact: Eases distribution pressure; supports range hold or bounce

items.title: US August PPI Due Today Amid Fed Hike Bets
items.summary: The August Producer Price Index lands at eight thirty Eastern this morning, with headline expected up point four percent month over month and five point three percent year over year, core up point three and four point six. This is the last major wholesale inflation read before next week's FOMC. Traders should care because a hot print would cement higher odds of a September rate hike after the strong jobs number, lifting yields and pressuring risk assets including crypto.
items.impact: Hot PPI boosts hike odds and yields, weighing on Bitcoin; soft print eases pressure

items.title: 10-Year Yields Hit Multi-Year Highs Despite Buyback
items.summary: The US ten-year Treasury yield climbed to around four point eight five percent, its highest since late twenty twenty three, after the Treasury announced a six billion dollar long-dated buyback that markets saw as too small. Oil above one hundred dollars and inflation fears from Middle East tensions added fuel. Crypto traders watch this closely because rising real yields tighten financial conditions and often correlate with risk-off moves in Bitcoin and equities.
items.impact: Higher yields pressure risk assets and crypto valuations

items.title: ECB Expected to Hike Rates 25bp Today
items.summary: The European Central Bank is widely expected to raise its deposit rate by a quarter point today as eurozone inflation hit three point three percent and energy prices surge from Middle East conflict. Focus will be on new projections and Lagarde's guidance for further hikes. This matters for global rates and the dollar, as synchronized central bank tightening can strengthen the greenback and weigh on crypto liquidity.
items.impact: Tighter euro policy supports DXY and adds global hawkish tilt

items.title: Oil Tops $100 on US-Iran Escalation, Inflation Fears Rise
items.summary: Brent crude pushed above one hundred dollars a barrel as US-Iran hostilities intensified with attacks on tankers and shipping routes. This revives energy-driven inflation concerns just ahead of US PPI and CPI. For crypto traders, higher oil feeds into sticky inflation narratives that keep the Fed hawkish, supporting yields and the dollar while challenging risk appetite.
items.impact: Energy shock raises inflation premium and rate hike probability

items.title: Fed September Hike Odds Near 60% After Strong Jobs
items.summary: Markets price roughly a sixty percent chance of a twenty-five basis point Fed hike at the September fifteen-sixteen meeting following the much stronger than expected August payrolls. Upcoming PPI and CPI will be decisive. Crypto should watch because a confirmed hike path would lift the dollar and real yields, typically a headwind for Bitcoin in the short term.
items.impact: Elevated hike odds tighten conditions for risk assets

items.title: Jobless Claims and Existing Home Sales Also Due Today
items.summary: Weekly initial jobless claims are expected around two hundred five thousand, near multi-decade lows, while August existing home sales are seen slipping to about three point nine eight million. Soft claims would reinforce labor strength and hike odds; weak home sales highlight rate sensitivity. These secondary prints still matter for the full picture ahead of the Fed decision and can swing intraday sentiment in rates and crypto.
items.impact: Labor strength supports hawkish Fed; housing softness shows rate pain

items.title: US-Iran tanker attacks push Brent oil above $100
items.summary: The United States destroyed multiple Iranian oil tankers after Iran targeted a US warship and commercial shipping near the Strait of Hormuz, in the biggest wave of attacks since the war began. Iran hit ships and fired missiles at a US base in Jordan. Brent crude settled over one hundred one dollars a barrel, the highest close in months, as supply fears mount with Hormuz flows already heavily disrupted. Traders should watch energy inflation pressure on rates and risk assets, plus further shipping risks that could keep volatility elevated.
items.impact: Higher energy costs and risk-off pressure on crypto and equities

items.title: Houthis seize Mocha port near Bab el-Mandeb Strait
items.summary: Iran-backed Houthi forces captured the strategic Red Sea port city of Mocha after days of fighting, pushing Saudi-backed government troops south and gaining leverage closer to the Bab el-Mandeb chokepoint. This follows Houthi strikes on Saudi cities and energy sites. With Hormuz already constrained, another key shipping lane under threat raises the odds of broader energy and trade disruptions. Crypto traders care because dual chokepoint risks amplify oil spikes and global risk aversion.
items.impact: Heightened Red Sea shipping risks and oil supply fears

items.title: IAEA board refers Iran to UN Security Council
items.summary: The IAEA board of governors voted to report Iran to the UN Security Council for the first time in twenty years over non-compliance with nuclear safeguards and lack of inspector access to key sites damaged in prior strikes. The resolution from the US, UK, France and Germany passed despite opposition from Russia and China. New sanctions face veto hurdles but the move escalates diplomatic pressure amid the ongoing war. It adds uncertainty that could sustain risk premiums in energy and markets.
items.impact: Diplomatic escalation without immediate new enforceable sanctions

items.title: Trump says Iran war ends right after US midterms
items.summary: President Trump stated the war with Iran will end immediately after the November midterms because Tehran cannot hold out longer and is trying to influence the vote. He linked high oil prices to the same timeline, saying they will tumble afterward, while noting more tanker strikes ahead. Advisers have privately warned the conflict could drag on longer. Markets will parse whether this is signaling a path to de-escalation or just political messaging amid elevated energy costs.
items.impact: Potential medium-term de-escalation hope mixed with near-term war continuation

items.title: Trump-Putin call as Zelensky plane nearly hit by drone
items.summary: Trump held what he called a great conversation with Putin focused on ending the Ukraine war quickly, with the Kremlin saying it could restore full US-Russia ties. Separately, Norwegian officials said a Russian drone nearly hit Zelensky's plane taking off from Moldova, delaying the flight amid airspace closures. Russian strikes continued killing civilians in Ukraine. Progress or stalemate in Ukraine talks remains a swing factor for broader risk sentiment and European energy dynamics.
items.impact: Ongoing Ukraine uncertainty with mixed diplomatic signals

items.title: Canada retaliatory tariffs on US goods take effect
items.summary: Canada's dollar-for-dollar counter-tariffs of up to fifty percent on roughly twenty-seven billion dollars of US goods, including steel, dairy, appliances and electronics, became effective after US Section 338 tariffs hit Canadian exports. The White House has adjusted some Canadian product scopes in response. This deepens the North American trade rift at a time of already elevated global inflation risks from energy. Traders monitor for spillover into growth outlooks and risk appetite.
items.impact: Trade friction adding to inflation and growth headwinds
